title: Which Job Is It?
instruction: Every recommender does three jobs. Which one is this mainly doing?

items.text: 'New this week from artists you've never heard of, but might like'
items.why: It surfaces what you wouldn't have searched for.

items.text: A reading app suggests an author you didn't know, because of the ones you love
items.why: Finding something new you couldn't have asked for is discovery.

items.text: Sorting 2,000 hotel results so that likely fits come first
items.why: It cuts a large list down to the few options worth your time.

items.text: A 'Start here' row in a catalogue of 100 million tracks
items.why: Without it, the catalogue is an unindexed library.
It sustains attention: good when it serves you, a problem when it doesn't.
Pure engagement: it brings you back, whatever you find there.

debrief: Discover, navigate, engage. The same row can serve more than one, and which job matters most depends on the product: navigation in a shop, discovery in media, engagement in social feeds.
